{"model": "llama3.2", "max_tokens": 300, "temperature": 1, "messages": [{"role": "system", "content": "Answer from the notes below and nothing else. Cite each note you use as [n]. If the notes do not answer, say so.

[1] (derivations.md) A write reaches every reader. When a handler writes a table, every session whose page read a derivation over that table renders again, so a reader sees another reader's change as it lands.

[2] (pages.md) A view is a function that answers elements: a stack of headings, paragraphs, fields and buttons. A field is bound to a fact, and a button names the handler its click runs.

[3] (derivations.md) A derivation over an external source stays fresh by its window: `fresh = 300` recomputes it at most every five minutes, and the default of zero means as fresh as the loop, recomputed every render."}, {"role": "user", "content": "how does a derivation stay fresh"}]}
